correctness.rationale: A unary type is an initial predecessor segment and a disjoint final successor segment, indexed by a discrete interval [i,j]. Homogeneity identifies the complete types from these finite diagrams. Two such intervals are disjoint exactly when a named element forces a strict comparison of the two new points; without that witness the specified incomparable extension is transitive and irreflexive and embeds over the base. In particular the diagonal is 1. For intervals [i,j],[k,l], the disjointness indicators 1[j<k] and 1[l<i] cannot both be 1, so the looped intersection indicator is 1 minus their sum. This separates the endpoints and proves the prescribed interior row relation. In the boundary basis with the full interval split off, the two families of boundary differences are isotropic with mixed block −1[j<i]; adjacent differences yield −1[i=j+1]. Each basis step is invertible over Z, including interior basis vectors with leading coefficient 1 on their own coordinate. This gives all radical vectors, the stated determinant of the boundary block, the Smith factors, and inertia/rank. At n=1 the interior basis is empty and the mixed block is (−1).
residual_risks: Read but did not rerun the recorded n≤9 congruence and n≤5 feasibility tests; the exact all-n proof was reconstructed.
